input.query: increase flow rate on the valve
what is the current flow rate
create a new document called notes
set the valve brightness to eighty
what is the weather in Brașov tomorrow
send an email to the team
add a rust dependency to Cargo.toml and update the lockfile

notes: Constructed by hand against the two real manifests. This is a fixture, not a benchmark: 30 queries is enough to expose a routing failure but far too few to measure an escalation rate with any confidence.

The three hit phrasings that deliberately share no vocabulary with the manifest ('shut the valve down now', 'stop the flow through valve-001', 'close the valve') are the interesting cases. If lexical matching passes all of them, no embedding model is needed. If it fails them, that failure set is the training set.

kind=negative with a real expect is the case that must NOT match. 'set the valve brightness to eighty' is the sharpest: it shares 'valve' with the actuator but describes a capability the manifest does not have.

'add a rust dependency to Cargo.toml' is included specifically because it is the query a coding agent would actually issue, and unia has no pattern for it. Correct behaviour is no match, not a wrong match.
